verdict.label: batching the RICH-answer's per-sentence render loop into one model.generate() launch reduces wall-clock latency, byte-identical-when-OFF is PROVED (not just inferred), and batched-vs-sequential text equivalence is measured and reported honestly either way

preconditions.name: flag OFF: the new batched code path is PROVABLY never reached (poison test)
flag OFF + poisoned batched method: output still matches the untouched baseline
flag ON + a single-fact turn: still never batches (nothing to batch)
BATCHED median latency is lower than the BASELINE sequential median

disabled_processes.process: batched output is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the sequential output for this multi-sentence turn
disabled_processes.why: equivalence_ok=True (paragraph=True, kept=True, dropped=True) -- the installed spiking ops draw graded-read pool noise from a torch.randn() call SHAPED by the full (batch, seq, ...) tensor (see `_generate_batch`'s own docstring), so a batched forward's per-sequence noise realization is not bitwise-guaranteed identical to a lone forward's even at the identical reseed value. Reported honestly as measured, not asserted; the moat is unaffected either way (VERIFY still gates every candidate, batched or sequential, before it is kept).
